figure_caption: Fig. 4. The etch rate over modification step duration a) for all studied materials, and b) enlarged for  $\mathrm{Al_2O_3}$ ,  $\mathrm{AlN_x}$ , and  $\mathrm{HfO_2}$ .
class:
a	multiple line chart
b	multiple line chart
summary:
a	The etch rate increases linearly for SiO2 and reaches an optimum for the other materials with the modification step duration, the only material that does not etch is TiN.
b	The etch rate initially increases, peaks at around 10 seconds, and then decreases for all materials.
q1: a	Can SiO2 be partially selective be etch with respect to any of the other materials, and if so, for which conditions?
a1: a	SiO2 has a way higher etch rate than for example HfO2, at 15 s of modification duration. This indicates that SiO2, at least partially, can selectively be etch with respect to HfO2.
q2: a	Which material has the highest etch resistance for these chemistries?
a2: a	TiN does not etch for any modification duration.
q3: b	What modification time is most likely used for industrial applications when etching AlNx?
a3: b	5 s of modification duration is most likely used as this would have similar etch results as longer times, but reduces the processing time.
q4: b	Is there only etching upon a modification step, and how can you tell?
a4: b	No there is continuous etching. For all three materials the etch rate is non-zero at 0 s modification duration.
